en.name: Morcilla
en.summary: Morcilla is a cooked Spanish blood sausage — the Burgos style bulked with rice, others with onion. It is cooked, not cured, so it is a perishable meat product: about 1 week refrigerated from purchase, and 1–2 months frozen. The numbers are borrowed from fully cooked smoked sausage links, as no agency publishes a morcilla timeline.
en.pantry: Morcilla does not keep at room temperature. It looks like a cured sausage and is not one: blood, fat and cooked rice or onion make a wet, nutrient-rich filling with nothing preserving it beyond the initial cooking. Out of the fridge it is bound by the two-hour rule, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F), and it should be cooked through before eating rather than sliced cold onto a board.
en.fridge: Keep morcilla at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in its wrapper and use it within about 1 week of purchase — Spanish hygiene rules put meat products from ungulates at 7 °C or below, and anything held more than a day belongs at 4 °C. Burgos-style morcilla is full of cooked rice as well as blood and fat, which makes it wetter and shorter-lived than a dry sausage, so treat the date on the pack as real rather than as a suggestion. Store it below ready-to-eat food and cook it through.
en.freezer: It freezes well for 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in whole links, wrapped tight with the air pressed out. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; past a couple of months the fat picks up freezer taint and the rice goes grainy. Thaw in the fridge and fry or bake it from cold — a frozen morcilla dropped straight into a hot pan bursts its casing.
en.thawing: Thaw overnight in the fridge, still wrapped, then cook it through. Never thaw on the counter, and do not refreeze a link that has thawed fully at room temperature.
spoilage: A sour or putrid smell when the wrapper comes off.
Slime on the casing or a sticky film on a cut face.
Mould anywhere — this is a cooked sausage and is not meant to carry a bloom.
A pack that is puffy, leaking or hissing when opened.
tips: Buy what you will cook in the week and freeze the rest in single links.
Take it out of a supermarket tray and wrap it properly if you are keeping it a few days.
Cook from chilled over moderate heat so the casing does not split.
If yours is hard and dry rather than soft and sliceable, it is a semi-dried style and behaves more like salchichón.

faq.q: How long does morcilla keep in the fridge?
faq.a: About 1 week from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or the date on the pack if that is sooner.

faq.q: Can you eat morcilla without cooking it?
faq.a: It is cooked in production, but it is a perishable product best cooked through before eating rather than served cold.
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in whole links. Thaw in the fridge and cook from cold so the casing does not burst.

zh.name: 西班牙血腸
zh.summary: Morcilla 是西班牙的熟製血腸——布爾戈斯式加米，其他版本加洋蔥。它是煮熟的，不是熟成風乾的，所以屬於易腐的肉製品：從購買日起算冷藏約 1 週，冷凍 1～2 個月。這些數字是借自「全熟煙燻香腸」，因為沒有機構公布過血腸的期限。
zh.pantry: 血腸不能放常溫。它外表像風乾香腸，但根本不是：血、油脂加上煮熟的米或洋蔥，是一份又濕又營養的內餡，除了製作時那一次加熱之外沒有任何保存機制。離開冰箱後受 2 小時原則規範，室溫超過 32 °C 時縮為 1 小時；吃之前要煮透，不要當冷盤切片直接上桌。
zh.fridge: 維持包裝放 4 °C 以下，購買後約 1 週內用完——西班牙的食品衛生規定把偶蹄類肉製品放在 7 °C 以下，存放超過一天的則歸到 4 °C。布爾戈斯式的血腸除了血和油脂還塞滿熟米，比乾式香腸更濕、也更短命，所以包裝上的日期請當真，不要當參考。放在即食食品下方，並且要煮透。
zh.freezer: 整條包緊、壓出空氣，在 −18 °C 下冷凍 1～2 個月效果不錯。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的；超過兩個月油脂會沾上冷凍庫的雜味，米粒口感變沙。請冷藏解凍，並從冰冷狀態下鍋煎或烤——冷凍狀態直接丟進熱鍋，腸衣會爆開。
zh.thawing: 維持包裝冷藏隔夜解凍，然後煮透。不要放室溫退冰；已在室溫下完全退冰的就不要再冷凍。
spoilage: 拆開包裝聞到酸敗或腐臭味。
腸衣發黏，或切面有一層黏膜。
任何部位長霉——這是熟製香腸，本來就不該有霉花。
包裝脹袋、滲液，或打開時發出洩氣聲。
tips: 買這一週煮得完的量，其餘一條一條冷凍。
要放好幾天的話，把超市托盤拆掉重新包好。
從冷藏狀態用中火慢煎，腸衣才不會裂。
如果你手上那條硬而乾、不好切軟片，那是半乾式的版本，性質比較接近西班牙風乾臘腸。

faq.q: 西班牙血腸冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下，從購買日起算約 1 週，若包裝日期更早則以包裝為準。

faq.q: 西班牙血腸可以不加熱直接吃嗎？
faq.a: 它在製作時已經煮熟，但仍是易腐品，建議煮透再吃，不要當冷盤。

faq.q: 西班牙血腸可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，整條在 −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。冷藏解凍後從冰冷狀態下鍋，腸衣才不會爆。
